ConnectionPolicy.description: Transport policy shared by every role.

application_name_prefix.description:
Each connection's `application_name` is this prefix and its role:
`lash/work`, `lash/renewal`, ... Default `lash`; 1 to 32 characters of
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

statement_cache_capacity.description:
Prepared statements each connection caches. Default 100 (SQLx's);
0 disables caching for a pooler that cannot carry them.

topology.description: How the endpoints reach the server.

transport.description: TLS settings that override the endpoint's own; none by default.

ConnectionTopology.description: How the endpoints reach the server.

oneOf.description:
Directly, or through a session-mode pooler: every connection is one
server session for its life. Roles install their guards as session
defaults as well as per transaction.

The primary endpoint is a transaction-mode pooler. Guards are
installed per transaction only, and every role that needs a session
of its own (the listeners, schema and sweep sessions, preflight and
migration) connects through the separate session endpoint.

DedicatedConnectionPolicy.description:
A role served by connections of its own, one per served node, that are
never recycled for idleness or age.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long opening (or reopening) the connection may take.

DeploymentBudget.description:
What a deployment runs beside one process's lash connections, for the
server-wide budget. The process's own connection count is derived from
the rest of the configuration, never entered by hand.

admin_headroom.description: Slots kept for administration; at least the server's reserved slots.

generations.description: Releases that overlap during a rollout; at least 2.

operator_connections.description: Operator pools that may overlap a process (preflight, migration).

other_clients.description: Other clients of the server, other databases' included.

other_host_connections.description: Other pools each process opens on the server (a host's own).

processes_per_generation.description: Processes of one release running at once.

retirement.description:
Required when `node` is supplied. Hosts can write
[`RetirementSettings::standard()`] as their explicit baseline.

GraphReadPolicy.description: Deployment graph-read admission, independent of write-side commit admission.

GuardPolicies.description: The guard profile of each kind of transaction.

durable.description:
Durable engine commits on the work and critical pools. Default lock
2 s, statement 5 s, idle 5 s, operation 10 s.

inspection.description:
Schema verification and preflight inspection. Default lock 5 s,
statement 30 s, idle 30 s, operation 30 s.

ordinary.description:
Store transactions and reads on the work pool. Default lock 10 s,
statement 30 s, idle 30 s, operation 60 s.

renewal.description:
Node registration and heartbeat. Default lock 250 ms, statement 1 s,
idle 1 s, operation 2 s; the operation deadline must be shorter than
the heartbeat interval.

replay.description:
Live replay and process replay transactions. Default lock 10 s,
statement 30 s, idle 30 s, operation 60 s.

scheduler.description:
Claims and the scheduler's other operations, which hold the node row
`FOR SHARE`. Default lock 250 ms, statement 1 s, idle 1 s, operation
2 s.

store_startup_ms.description:
The whole store open: capacity check, pools, schema verification.
Default 30 s.

LiveReplayPolicy.description: The live replay store: its data, its data pool and its own listener.

listener.description: The replay listener's own session. Default 5 s acquire.

pool.description:
Publication, reads, cleanup and reloads. Default 7 connections, 5 s
acquire, no checkout ping.

reconnect.description: Default 100 ms to 5 s with jitter.

MaintenancePolicy.description: Operator work and the store's detached sessions.

checkpoint_ref_chunk.description:
Checkpoint refs/bodies in one query; standard 16,384 (around 1 MiB
of hash text). No workload measurement establishes this chunk size.

max_schema_sessions.description: Schema verification sessions open at once per storage. Default 1.

max_sweep_sessions.description: Attachment sweep sessions open at once per storage. Default 1.

migration_batch_rows.description: Rows one backfill batch moves. Default 500.

migration_deadline_ms.description: The whole migration job's deadline. Default none.

migration_lock_timeout_ms.description: How long a migration waits for the schema lock. Default 30 s.

migration_pool.description: `lash migrate`'s pool. Default 2 connections, 30 s acquire.

preflight_pool.description: A preflight probe's pool. Default 2 connections, 5 s acquire.

process_event_release_page_rows.description: Rows one process-event release page reads. Default 256.

sweep_liveness_probe_timeout_ms.description: The sweep's liveness probe lock wait. Default 500 ms.

PoolPolicy.description: A pooled role's sizing and recycling.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long a checkout may wait, connecting included.

idle_timeout_ms.description:
Close a connection idle this long; `null` never closes it for
idleness.

max_connections.description: The most connections the pool opens; at least 1.

max_lifetime_ms.description: Recycle a connection this old; `null` never recycles it for age.

min_connections.description: Connections kept open while idle; at most `max_connections`.

test_before_acquire.description:
Ping every connection before handing it out. Default false: only a
connection idle for 10 s or longer is pinged, so a checkout on the
hot path costs no round trip.

PostgresNameLimits.description:
Host name admission within PostgreSQL's 63-byte identifier space. The
remaining bytes are reserved for connection-role and channel suffixes.

ProcessReplayDataPolicy.description:
Where the process replay store keeps its tables, how it batches and what
it retains. The retention values are a provisional preset: no measurement
backs them.

A process's window is cut by whichever bound it reaches first, so the
replay it can offer lasts about
`min(max_age, max_events / events per second, max_bytes / bytes per second)`.

cleanup_batch.description: Rows one cleanup statement reclaims. Default 256, 1 to 65536.

cleanup_interval_ms.description:
How often a replica reclaims expired events, idle windows and unused
reservations, and counts the processes its subscribers follow as
accessed: a followed process keeps its window while this plus
`cleanup_jitter` is below `max_age`. Default 30 s, 100 ms to 1 h.

cleanup_jitter_ms.description:
The most a cleanup run is delayed past its interval, drawn at random.
Default 10 s; at most the interval.

max_age_ms.description:
How long an event stays replayable, whether or not the process has
ended. Default 120 s, 1 ms to 24 h.

max_batch_events.description:
The events a tick gathers into one transaction; a single
publication is never split. Default 1024, 1 to 65536.

max_bytes_per_process.description:
Encoded bytes retained per process; a larger single publication is
refused. Default 8 MiB, 1 KiB to 1 GiB.

max_events_per_process.description: Events retained per process. Default 2048, 1 to 1,000,000.

max_pending_bytes.description:
Encoded bytes a replica holds between `publish` and their tick; a
publisher past it waits. Default 16 MiB, 1 KiB to 1 GiB.

max_pending_events.description:
Events a replica holds between `publish` and their tick; a publisher
past it waits. Default 8192, 1 to 1,000,000.

max_processes.description:
Processes with a window at once, across every replica; the idlest
window is evicted to admit another. Default 4096, 1 to 1,000,000.

max_retained_bytes.description:
Encoded bytes reserved across every process's window, across every
replica. Default 256 MiB; `max_bytes_per_process` to 1 TiB.

publish_concurrency.description:
Publish transactions at once. Default 4; 1 to the data pool's
`max_connections`.

publish_tick_ms.description:
How long a replica gathers publications before one transaction
writes them. Default 5 ms, 0 to 1 s.

reservation_bytes.description:
The step a process's share of `max_retained_bytes` grows and shrinks
by: a window takes the aggregate lock once per step, not per event.
Default 64 KiB; 1 KiB to `max_bytes_per_process`.

schema.description:
The schema holding the tables; `<schema>_process_replay` names the
notification channel. Default `lash_process_replay`; a lowercase
identifier of at most 48 characters.

ProcessReplayPolicy.description:
The process replay store: its data, its data pool and its own listener.
It shares nothing with the live replay store.

listener.description: The process replay listener's own session. Default 5 s acquire.

pool.description:
Publication, reads and cleanup. Default 7 connections, 5 s acquire,
no checkout ping.

reconnect.description: Default 100 ms to 5 s with jitter.

ReconnectPolicy.description: How a lost listener session is reopened.

initial_delay_ms.description: The first wait after a lost session; each failed attempt doubles it.

jitter.description: Draw each wait at random from its upper half.

ReplayDataPolicy.description:
Where the live replay store keeps its tables, how it batches and what it
retains.

cleanup_batch.description: Rows one cleanup statement reclaims. Default 256, 1 to 65536.

cleanup_interval_ms.description:
How often a replica reclaims expired events and idle sessions, and
counts the sessions its subscribers follow as accessed: a followed
session keeps its window while this plus `cleanup_jitter` is below
`max_age`. Default 30 s, 100 ms to 1 h.

cleanup_jitter_ms.description:
The most a cleanup run is delayed past its interval, drawn at random.
Default 10 s; at most the interval.

max_age_ms.description: How long an event stays replayable. Default 120 s, 1 ms to 24 h.

max_batch_events.description:
The events a tick gathers into one transaction; a single
publication is never split. Default 1024, 1 to 65536.

max_bytes_per_session.description:
Encoded bytes retained per session; a larger single publication is
refused. Default 8 MiB, 1 KiB to 1 GiB.

max_events_per_session.description: Events retained per session. Default 2048, 1 to 1,000,000.

publish_concurrency.description:
Publish transactions at once. Default 4; 1 to the data pool's
`max_connections`.

publish_tick_ms.description:
How long a replica gathers publications before one transaction
writes them. Default 5 ms, 0 to 1 s.

schema.description:
The schema holding the tables; it also names the notification
channel. Default `lash_live_replay`; a lowercase identifier of at
most 48 characters.

ReplaySchemaMode.description: Whether a replay store creates its tables or only checks them.

oneOf.description:
Create the schema and its tables when absent, from the published
DDL verbatim. Needs `CREATE` on the database.

Run no DDL: the host applied the published artifact itself. Absent
or different tables refuse the connect.

RetryPolicies.description: The retry policy of each kind of database work.

durable.description:
Contended durable owner and mailbox commits. Default 4 attempts, 5
to 20 ms.

live_replay.description:
Contended live replay publications and trims. Default 8 attempts,
5 to 100 ms.

process_replay.description:
Contended process replay publications and trims. Default 8
attempts, 5 to 100 ms.

store.description:
Contended store maintenance transactions. Default 4 attempts, 5 to
20 ms.

wait_resolution.description:
Contended wait resolutions and due-wait settlements. Default 3
attempts, 5 to 20 ms.

RetryPolicy.description:
A bounded retry of database work whose attempt is known to have rolled
back, run by [`RetryPolicy::run`] around one complete, immutable
transaction. Never a retry of a tool or model call, and never of a
`COMMIT` whose outcome is unknown.

attempts.description: Attempts, the first included; at least 1.

initial_delay_ms.description: The pause before the second attempt; each later pause doubles it.

jitter.description:
Draw each pause at random from its upper half, so contending
writers do not retry in step.

max_delay_ms.description: The longest pause; at least the initial delay.

RolePolicies.description:
Each role's capacity.

The routing is lash's, not the host's: node registration and heartbeat
run on the renewal connections; claim, adoption, owned scans, node drain
and liveness probes on the scheduler pool; reap, node release, hand-back
and every cancel and terminal commit on the critical pool; everything
else on the work pool.

critical.description:
Reap, release, hand-back, cancels and terminals. Default 3
connections, 2 s acquire.

listener.description:
The notification listener, one session per served node, which also
holds the node's liveness lock. Default 2 s acquire.

max_store_operations.description:
Durable engine operations on the work pool at once; the rest of the
work pool serves store API calls. Admission is taken before checkout
and released with the connection, never held across a tool or model
body. Default 16; 1 to `work.max_connections`.

renewal.description: Lease renewal: one connection per served node. Default 500 ms acquire.

scheduler.description: Claims, adoption, liveness. Default 1 connection, 500 ms acquire.

served_nodes.description:
Nodes this process serves over one storage; each has its own renewal
connection and listener session. Default 1.

work.description:
Store calls and ordinary durable commits. Default 16 connections,
30 s acquire.

SchemaCheck.description:
What a [`crate::PostgresStorage`] does when the live schema does not match
the shape this build expects.

The default is [`SchemaCheck::Enforce`]: a mismatch is a hard error at open,
because the guards it protects (the exactly-once dedup unique index, the
cascade foreign keys) fail silently rather than loudly when they are absent.
[`SchemaCheck::WarnOnly`] exists for the one failure this crate cannot rule
out by testing — a bug in the expectation artifact itself against a
PostgreSQL build lash has not seen. It is deliberately an API-level choice a
host commits to in reviewed code, never an environment variable an operator
can flip at 3am.

# What no `SchemaCheck` relaxes

This governs the catalog comparison and nothing else. Two preconditions sit
outside it:

- **The component version stamp.** It is the supported-range boundary
  (FIG-3797): a stamp outside `[MIN_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION,
  SCHEMA_VERSION]` is refused unconditionally, whichever direction it
  differs in, so a valve adopted for a structural false positive cannot
  silently run one build against another schema generation.
- **The catalog identity row.** Without it there is no identity to hand
  the session catalogs open builds, so there is nothing for open to return:
  no identity, no store.

The `lash_process_change_clock` seed row is deliberately *not* in that list.
It is reported as an ordinary finding, so [`SchemaCheck::WarnOnly`] opens
without it and every process-registry write then fails at runtime. The
asymmetry is not that one row matters more than the other — both are required
— it is that the identity is something open must physically read and hand back,
while the clock row is only something writes will later need. A valve that
could not be overridden for the clock row would be a valve that cannot be used
to work around a checker bug, which is its entire purpose.

oneOf.description: Reject the open with a per-object diff when the live schema drifts.

SignalPolicy.description:
The durable notification listener's policy. Durable polling stays
authoritative while a listener reconnects.

reconnect.description: Default 250 ms to 5 s with jitter.

TransactionGuards.description: The limits one kind of transaction runs under.

idle_in_transaction_timeout.description:
`idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`: the longest a transaction
may sit idle; the server ends the session after it.

lock_timeout.description: `lock_timeout`: the longest one lock wait, the first one included.

operation_deadline_ms.description:
The client's bound on the whole operation: admission, checkout,
every statement and commit. `null` only for explicit operator work.

transaction_timeout.description:
`transaction_timeout` (PostgreSQL 17+): the longest whole
transaction; the server ends the session after it.

TransportOverrides.description:
TLS settings applied over the endpoint's. An absent value keeps the
endpoint's own.

ssl_client_cert.description: The client certificate file; given together with `ssl_client_key`.

ssl_client_key.description: The client key file; given together with `ssl_client_cert`.

ssl_mode.description: The TLS mode; production hosts usually want `verify_full`.

description:
Every lash PostgreSQL connection role's sizes, guards, retries and
names, and the durable node settings, validated together.

deployment.description:
The deployment's connection budget. `None` skips the server
capacity check. Both presets leave this optional; a host can declare it.

guards.description: SQL guards and whole-operation deadlines, by operation role.

live_replay.description: The live replay store; `None` opens no replay pool or listener.

node.description:
The durable substrate's parameters, the node lease's included. The
durable backend takes them from here and from nowhere else.

process_replay.description:
The process replay store; `None` opens no process replay pool or
listener.

retry.description: Bounded retries of known-aborted database work.

roles.description: Each pooled and dedicated role's capacity.

schema_check.description: What open does when the live schema drifts.

signals.description: The durable notification listener's reconnect policy.
